diff --git a/broker/vm/ASSUMPTIONS.md b/broker/vm/ASSUMPTIONS.md
index b9f51411f..9992730fe 100644
--- a/broker/vm/ASSUMPTIONS.md
+++ b/broker/vm/ASSUMPTIONS.md
@@ -41,3 +41,4 @@ package, that a reviewer may want to change.
 | V32 | **runsc's own messages never reach the guest (SR2-3h, SR2-3m, SR2-3n).** In runsc release-20260928.0, `util.Errorf` (and `Fatalf`, exit 128) always writes its message to stderr and, when `--log` is set, a JSON error line to that file; info lines go only to `--debug-log` (else discarded); the guest's in-sandbox pid is written to `--internal-pid-file` only after the command starts (read from `runsc/cmd/util/util.go`, `runsc/cli/cli.go`, `runsc/cmd/exec.go` at that tag). `runsc exec`'s stderr is the guest command's too, so `--log` alone cannot keep runsc's text off it. `gvisor.Exec` gives each exec its own `--log` and `--debug-log` files (0600, removed after) and treats the exec as runsc's failure when that `--log` is non-empty or the pid file is empty: it answers an error and no output (not a result, so the guest's exit code and stderr are never runsc's), and the worker tools turn that error into a ref (workers K21). The failure's messages (error log, debug log, stderr, each clipped to 16 KiB) go to `exec.log` in the runsc state directory (broker-held, 0700), 0600, rotated at 1 MiB to `exec.log.1` through `keepConsole`, so the two stay within 2 MiB plus one entry. A successful exec logs nothing. A Go runtime panic, fatal error or fatal signal (`SIGxxx:` and `PC=`) in runsc after the guest started writes its trace to runsc's fd 2 with no `--log` line (runsc's `--panic-log-fd` is refused for non-internal commands) and exits 2. So the guest's stderr is not runsc's fd 2 (SR2-3n): `gvisor.Exec` passes a pipe of its own as runsc's fd 3 with `exec --pass-fd 3:2`, which in that release sets the guest's fd 2 to the host fd 3 over the default `os.Stderr` (`fdMap[mapping.Guest] = file` in `runsc/cmd/exec.go`; `FDMappings.Set` in `runsc/cmd/sandboxsetup/fdmappings.go` refuses only negative numbers), and reads runsc's own fd 2, clipped to 16 KiB, apart. No guest write can then split, mimic or crowd out runsc's trace, and none of runsc's stderr reaches the guest; Exec treats as runsc's failure any failed exec with anything on runsc's own stderr (any non-zero exit, a kill, or `ErrWaitDelay`), read before or after its context ended (Security S1 on #391, V34, P1-4-flake-crashed); an exit 0 with text stays a result, and logs that stream's first 16 KiB. A guest that exits 2 keeps its output whatever it wrote, a Go program's own panic included. The guest's stderr pipe is read to its end but no longer than `ExecWaitDelay` past the context's end or runsc's exit, as os/exec bounds stdout. Known gaps: a guest command that cannot start (a missing program) reads as fixed text, not runsc's (V33, SR2-3p); and runsc verbs other than `exec` still put stderr in their errors, which reach the guest only as refs (SR2-3g's filter, workers K21). | RES-4, CAP-8 | A fixed-text sentinel for a command that did not start; re-read the four files when the pinned runsc changes (V20); a runsc that ignored `--pass-fd 3:2` would put the guest's stderr on runsc's stream, which Exec never answers, so it would withhold output, not leak runsc's text; CI's `TestIntegrationWorkerExec` runs the pinned runsc and fails if the guest's stderr does not arrive through Exec's pipe. Any byte on runsc's own stderr now withholds the output of every failed exec, an ordinary non-zero guest exit included, so this rests on runsc writing nothing to its stderr on a normal exec; `TestIntegrationWorkerExec` (guest exits 3) checks that against the pinned runsc, and P1-4-flake-runsc-recheck re-checks it at the next bump. |
 | V33 | **Exec's runtime failure is a bare sentinel (SR2-3j, release finding 362-2).** When runsc fails, `gvisor.Exec` answers a bare sentinel naming no path; the detail is in the exec log (V32). With a pid written, it is `vm.ErrExecFailed` (the command may have run; a runsc panic after the start included, V32). With none, the pid file alone does not show the command never ran, since runsc writes it after the start (SR2-3q), so `notRun` reads runsc's first `--log` line (JSON, at most 1 MiB): `vm.ErrExecNotStarted` only when it starts with one of the messages runsc's exec writes before the start (`loading container failed: `, `parsing process spec: `, `executing processes for container: `, from `runsc/cmd/exec.go` at the pinned tag); within the last, a lost answer from the sandbox (`in sandbox: urpc method "`, from `pkg/urpc/urpc.go`: the call was sent and may have started the command) is `vm.ErrExecFailed`; and `vm.ErrExecNoProgram` (SR2-3p) when the line ends with the sentry's error for the broker's own `argv[0]`: `failed to load <path>: <errno>` (`pkg/sentry/loader/loader.go`; the path is `argv[0]`, `path.Join("/", argv[0])` for a relative path, or a PATH directory's entry for a bare name) or `error finding executable <%q name> in PATH [<dirs>]: <errno>` (`pkg/sentry/fsimpl/user/path.go`), with errno ENOENT, EACCES, ENOEXEC or ENOTDIR. Any other line, or none (runsc killed, or panicking before the pid write), is `vm.ErrExecFailed`. A guest's argv appears in the line only after runsc's prefix and, in the sandbox call's `%q` of its arguments, with every quote escaped; the not-found match is anchored at the line's end, where the sentry's error is, and no other sentry error ends in guest text, so a guest cannot make a failure read as not started; an argv that reads as a lost answer only makes it `ErrExecFailed`. Known gaps: an `argv[0]` that is not valid UTF-8 (JSON replaces it) or a PATH directory holding a space, quote or colon reads as `ErrExecNotStarted` rather than `ErrExecNoProgram`. A cancelled context still answers the context's error. | CAP-8 | Re-read those five files when the pinned runsc changes (V20). |
 | V34 | **A deadline answers partial output unless runsc wrote (P1-4-flake).** When Exec's context ends while runsc still runs, Exec kills it, so its exit is the kill's (-1), never 2. If runsc's own stderr then holds anything, Exec treats the exec as runsc's failure (no output, the trace in `exec.log`), since that stream carries only runsc's text (V32, SR2-3n): a runsc that panicked just before the deadline is not answered as the guest's partial output. runsc killed from outside (a cgroup OOM kill) after writing to its stderr, with the context alive, exits -1 too and is the same failure (P1-4-flake-crashed); killed before writing anything, it still answers a result with `ExitCode` -1 (P1-4-flake-oomquiet). If it holds nothing, the guest's partial output stands with the context's error, and `vm.Manager.Exec` answers it as `TimedOut` (CAP-8): a deadline alone is not runsc's failure. Withholding errs only toward losing output; the guest cannot write runsc's stream. | CAP-8, RES-4 | If runsc ever writes non-failure text to its stderr during an exec, a deadline would lose the guest's partial output, and so would every failed exec, an ordinary non-zero guest exit included (V32); re-read with V32's files when the pinned runsc changes (V20). |
+| V35 | **runsc's exit 128 is runsc's fatal, not the guest's (P1-4-flake-exit128).** In runsc release-20260928.0, `runsc exec` reaches `util.Fatalf` (exit 128, its message on stderr and as a `--log` JSON line) on three paths: `loading container failed: `, `parsing process spec: ` and `failure to start child exec process`; its ordinary failures are `util.Errorf` (exit 1). Each of these runs before runsc writes the pid file (V32, SR2-3q); the third is the detached exec's path, which neither `Exec` nor the corpus replay takes. Through `gvisor.Exec` such a fatal is already a failure (V32, V33): the empty pid file withholds the output, logs runsc's text to `exec.log`, and `notRun` reads the `--log` line's prefix and answers `vm.ErrExecNotStarted` (`TestRunscFatalExit128AnswersNoOutput`, a pinning test with the fake's `fatal128`; the fake's `prestart` pins the same in `notstarted_test.go`). Any runsc text after the pid write, whatever the exit, answers `vm.ErrExecFailed` instead (V32, the fake's `latepanic`). A guest's own exit 128 with runsc silent stays a result (`TestGuestExit128WithoutRunscTextIsAResult`), so no rule may key on the code 128 alone. `TestCorpusReplayInAMachine` still runs a raw `runsc exec` (not `Exec`, whose `--cwd`, `--user` and `--pass-fd` differ: a release row of its own); its error now carries the exit code, the last 2 KiB of the process's stderr (runsc's merged with the guest's, since the raw exec passes no `--pass-fd`, and labelled so) and the last 2 KiB of a `--log` file of its own, which is runsc's alone (`rawExec`), so its intermittent exit 128 on #584, #588 and #569 names runsc's reason the next time. The cause of those is unproven (container load under contention, or a child start failing under load); no retry, and no serialising of the machine tests, until that text shows it. | CAP-8, RES-4 | If the stderr shows resource exhaustion or contention, a release row serialises the machine tests in `ci.yml`; if runsc documents the fatal as transient, a retry that logs every attempt. Re-read `runsc/cmd/exec.go` and `runsc/cmd/util/util.go` when the pinned runsc changes (V20). |
diff --git a/broker/vm/gvisor/corpus_test.go b/broker/vm/gvisor/corpus_test.go
index 2427b5ab4..e48534b2c 100644
--- a/broker/vm/gvisor/corpus_test.go
+++ b/broker/vm/gvisor/corpus_test.go
@@ -1,6 +1,7 @@
 package gvisor
 
 import (
+	"bytes"
 	"context"
 	"encoding/json"
 	"errors"
@@ -502,12 +503,81 @@ func TestCorpusReplayInAMachine(t *testing.T) {
 	r.create(x.machine, admission.Accepted)
 	r.ask(x.machine, "token") // waits for the machine to start
 	x.sock = vm.ServicesMount + "/" + guest.Socket
+	logs := t.TempDir()
 	x.run = func(ctx context.Context, args ...string) (string, error) {
-		out, err := r.rt.cmd(ctx, append([]string{"exec", cid(x.machine), "/guest"}, args...)...).Output()
+		out, err := rawExec(ctx, r.rt, logs, x.machine, append([]string{"/guest"}, args...)...)
 		if ctx.Err() != nil {
 			err = ctx.Err()
 		}
-		return strings.TrimSpace(string(out)), err
+		return strings.TrimSpace(out), err
 	}
 	replayAll(t, x)
 }
+
+// rawExecTail is how much of runsc's stderr and of its --log a failed raw
+// exec's error carries.
+const rawExecTail = 2048
+
+// rawExec runs argv in machine id with a raw `runsc exec`, as the corpus
+// replay always has, and answers its stdout. It does not go through
+// Runtime.Exec, whose --cwd, --user and --pass-fd differ (a release row
+// of its own). It adds only a --log file of its own, in dir, and keeps
+// the process's stderr: when the exec fails, the error carries the exit
+// code and the last rawExecTail bytes of each, since an exit 128 is
+// runsc's own fatal and its reason is only there (P1-4-flake-exit128).
+// With no --pass-fd, that stderr is runsc's merged with the guest's, and
+// its label says so; the --log file is runsc's alone. The text is from
+// synthetic corpus runs, printed only in a test failure.
+func rawExec(ctx context.Context, r *Runtime, dir, id string, argv ...string) (string, error) {
+	f, err := os.CreateTemp(dir, "exec-*.log")
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", err
+	}
+	f.Close()
+	defer os.Remove(f.Name())
+	var stderr bytes.Buffer
+	c := r.cmd(ctx, append([]string{"--log=" + f.Name(), "exec", cid(id)}, argv...)...)
+	c.Stderr = &stderr
+	out, err := c.Output()
+	if exit, ok := err.(*exec.ExitError); ok {
+		log, _ := os.ReadFile(f.Name())
+		err = fmt.Errorf("%w (exit %d)\nrunsc and guest stderr: %q\nrunsc log: %q", exit, exit.ExitCode(), tail(stderr.Bytes(), rawExecTail), tail(log, rawExecTail))
+	}
+	return string(out), err
+}
+
+// tail answers b's last n bytes.
+func tail(b []byte, n int) string { return string(b[max(0, len(b)-n):]) }
+
+// REQ: CAP-8, RES-4
+//
+// P1-4-flake-exit128: the corpus replay's raw `runsc exec` failed with a
+// bare "exit status 128", runsc's own fatal, its reason discarded. Its
+// error now carries the exit code and the tails of runsc's stderr and
+// --log, so the next occurrence names runsc's reason.
+func TestRawExecErrorCarriesRunscText(t *testing.T) {
+	r := fakeRunsc(t)
+	_, err := rawExec(context.Background(), r, t.TempDir(), "corpus", "fatal128")
+	var exit *exec.ExitError
+	if !errors.As(err, &exit) || exit.ExitCode() != 128 {
+		t.Fatalf("error %v, want runsc's exit 128", err)
+	}
+	msg := err.Error()
+	for _, want := range []string{"exit 128", "runsc and guest stderr: ", "runsc log: "} {
+		if !strings.Contains(msg, want) {
+			t.Errorf("error lacks %q: %s", want, msg)
+		}
+	}
+	// Once from stderr, once from the --log line.
+	if n := strings.Count(msg, "loading container failed: "+runscCanary); n != 2 {
+		t.Errorf("runsc's message %d times in the error, want 2: %s", n, msg)
+	}
+}
+
+// Only the tail of runsc's text is kept, so a large stderr cannot flood
+// the test log.
+func TestRawExecErrorClipsRunscText(t *testing.T) {
+	if got := tail([]byte(strings.Repeat("x", 3*rawExecTail)+"end"), rawExecTail); len(got) != rawExecTail || !strings.HasSuffix(got, "end") {
+		t.Fatalf("tail kept %d bytes ending %q", len(got), got[max(0, len(got)-8):])
+	}
+}
diff --git a/broker/vm/gvisor/panic_test.go b/broker/vm/gvisor/panic_test.go
index ba238feb9..40c2ab0d4 100644
--- a/broker/vm/gvisor/panic_test.go
+++ b/broker/vm/gvisor/panic_test.go
@@ -291,3 +291,42 @@ func TestGuestNonZeroExitWithoutRunscTextIsAResult(t *testing.T) {
 		t.Fatalf("a guest's exit was logged:\n%s", b)
 	}
 }
+
+// runsc's util.Fatalf exits 128 with a --log line and its message on
+// stderr (P1-4-flake-exit128): runsc's failure, not the guest's exit 128.
+// runsc's exec calls Fatalf only before the pid write, so Exec answers
+// ErrExecNotStarted (notRun), not ErrExecFailed. Pinning: true at main
+// through Exec; the corpus replay's raw exec is what lost the message.
+func TestRunscFatalExit128AnswersNoOutput(t *testing.T) {
+	r := fakeRunsc(t)
+	res, err := r.Exec(context.Background(), "wk-1", vm.Command{Argv: []string{"fatal128"}, MaxOutput: 4096})
+	if err != vm.ErrExecNotStarted {
+		t.Fatalf("error %v, want %v; result %+v", err, vm.ErrExecNotStarted, res)
+	}
+	if len(res.Stdout) > 0 || len(res.Stderr) > 0 || res.ExitCode != 0 {
+		t.Fatalf("runsc's fatal answered output: %+v", res)
+	}
+	b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(r.StateDir, "exec.log"))
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if !strings.Contains(string(b), "loading container failed: "+runscCanary) {
+		t.Errorf("exec log lacks runsc's fatal:\n%s", b)
+	}
+}
+
+// The control: a guest's own exit 128, with runsc silent, stays a result,
+// so not every 128 is withheld.
+func TestGuestExit128WithoutRunscTextIsAResult(t *testing.T) {
+	r := fakeRunsc(t)
+	res, err := r.Exec(context.Background(), "wk-1", vm.Command{Argv: []string{"exit128"}})
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if res.ExitCode != 128 || string(res.Stdout) != "guest out\n" {
+		t.Fatalf("guest's own exit 128: %+v", res)
+	}
+	if b, _ := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(r.StateDir, "exec.log")); len(b) > 0 {
+		t.Fatalf("a guest's exit was logged:\n%s", b)
+	}
+}
